MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  AUGUST 24, 2021

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 7:01 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Flag salute led by Daniel Sabet of Cub Scout Pack 970.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

NONE.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF suggested adding the subject of Assembly Bill 215 to item 8B
within the City Council Minutes, Consent Calendar item number 5E.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-G AS FOLLOWS BY
  THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF AUGUST 2021

  APPROVED WARRANTS 64200 THROUGH 64256 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $400,717.64 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 080121 THROUGH
  080221 IN THE AMOUNT OF $100,590.99 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF $501,308.63 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
AUGUST 24, 2021
 C.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF JULY 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF JULY 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF AUGUST 10, 2021

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

F.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF AUGUST 16, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  PALOS VERDES PENINSULA PUBLIC SAFETY COMMITTEE AND REGIONAL
  CONTRACT LAW ENFORCEMENT COMMITTEE MINUTES OF MAY 13, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN requested to move Item 8B to be heard next, before item 8A.

B.  AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT (ARPA) FUNDING OPPORTUNITIES AND
  REQUEST TO APPROVE A WILLDAN ENGINEERING CONTRACT FOR THE
  MARLOMA NEIGHBORHOOD FOR AN INITIAL SEPTIC TO SEWER STUDY USING
  A PORTION OF ARPA FUNDS

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF suggested the Council discuss and consider the possibility of using
ARPA funds in a way that would help the local businesses and residents.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN summarized that a decision must be made as to whether or not the
City’s upfront cost of $130,000 should be reimbursed by the future sewer district. He further
explained that if the City is reimbursed by the sewer district, ARPA funds could not be used,
and undesignated General Funds would need to be used instead. If the City is not reimbursed,
the City could use ARPA funds.

Ron Stein, Willdan Engineering Project Manager summarized the proposal for the project.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba stated that whether or not to
accept the $30,000 contribution from the residents should be decided this evening, in
response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

Kathleen McGowan of McGowan Consulting summarized several financial resources that
may be available to the City for septic to sewer projects, including $200 million through the
State Water Resources Control Board under the Budget Act of 2021 that is available for
water and wastewater projects including septic to sewer funding. She also explained grant
opportunities with the Clean Water State Revolving fund.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
AUGUST 24, 2021
 MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN inquired about the specific information the community
knows regarding the formation of a district. Consultant Stein explained the workshop that
was held where preliminary information was shared with the community, and that the
preliminary sewer study proposed this evening would give the community further information
needed in order to make an informed decision.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN expressed concern about the possibility of the final project
cost going beyond the preliminary project estimates.

Resident Robert Hladek spoke on behalf of the Marloma Homeowner’s Association, noting
that the residents are aware of the history of the project and the status of this study, and that
currently 31 of the 57 homeowners have committed to contribute their own funds to support
this study.

Resident Jay Gample echoed Mr. Hladek’s comments, emphasizing concerns about the
many septic systems reaching their end of life.

Consultant McGowan explained that when these systems do eventually fail, residents would
be required to replace them with an advanced septic system which can be very costly, in
response COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA. COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA stated that she
would be in favor of conducting the study, whether or not a district is formed, with the study’s
data being of value today and in the future.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  AUTHORIZE THE WILLDAN STUDY USING THE COMMUNITY’S $30,000
  DONATION, WHETHER OR NOT THE CITY IS REIMBURSED.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired if the reimbursability of the funds must be decided upon
now. City Attorney Davis stated that this could be decided upon in a future discussion.

Mr. Hladek noted that the homeowners are aware that their contribution of funds are funds
at risk if the vote fails, which to him is reflective of the community’s commitment.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted that the information derived from the study will
always exist, which Mr. Stein confirmed, noting that only minor cost adjustments would be
needed for future construction costs.

City Manager Grammer summarized that if Council would like to be reimbursed for the
$130,000 cost of the study, then it would be appropriate to assign General Funds and if the
district is approved then the City’s costs would be reimbursed. If the City Council is interested
is using ARPA funds, the City would not be reimbursed.

City Manager Grammer stated that with Council direction, the City could allocate General
Funds to complete the study, apply for applicable grants, and if successful in receiving the
grants then the City would not need to be reimbursed.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA confirmed that if the district doesn’t get formed, the City
may still be able to be reimbursed by the State grant.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No additional public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVED AN INITIAL SEPTIC TO SEWER STUDY FOR THE MARLOMA
  NEIGHBORHOOD IN THE AMOUNT OF $109,526 USING AMERICAN
  RESCUE PLAN ACT (ARPA) FUNDING OR OTHER REIMBURSABLE GRANT
  FUNDING WITH THE UNDERSTANDING THE MARLOMA NEIGHBORHOOD
  WILL PROVIDE FUNDS IN THE AMOUNT $30,000 TOWARD THE STUDY.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
AUGUST 24, 2021
   AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

Discussion ensued regarding the various ways they City could use the available ARPA funds,
specifically as relief for local business owners.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN summarized the Council’s consensus to have staff contact the Harbor
Sight Neighborhood to determine interest for the Septic to Sewer Project Assistance, using
either grant funding, ARPA funds or general funds.

Consultant McGowan explained the Montecillo Storm Drain Dry Well project in detail,
highlighting the project’s urgency regarding the City’s compliance requirements for stormwater.

City Manager Grammer summarized that staff is seeking direction from Council for a project
roadmap for use of the ARPA funds, and that all projects decided upon will come back to
Council for further discussion and direction.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF recommended the Council approve the four proposed projects
within the staff report directing staff to seek grants to fund them, freeing up the ARPA funds to
be used toward businesses and residents recovering from COVID.

Discussion continued regarding options for the use of the ARPA funds.

As a point of order, City Manager Grammer noted that a motion was needed to specifically
approve the Task Order for Willdan’s proposal as presented.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE A TASK ORDER UNDER WILLDAN'S PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT FOR THE PREVIOUS MOTION APPROVING AN INITIAL
  SEPTIC TO SEWER STUDY FOR THE MARLOMA NEIGHBORHOOD IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $109,526 USING AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT (ARPA)
  FUNDING OR OTHER REIMBURSABLE GRANT FUNDING WITH THE
  UNDERSTANDING THE MARLOMA NEIGHBORHOOD WILL PROVIDE
  FUNDS IN THE AMOUNT $30,000 TOWARD THE STUDY.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

Consensus of Council to:

  DIRECT STAFF TO RETURN WITH A SCOPE OF WORK AND PROPOSAL
  FOR THE STORM DRAIN DRY WELLS PROJECT; AND DIRECT STAFF TO
  EXPLORE USING THE AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT (ARPA) FUNDING
  FOR COVID-RELATED BUSINESS ASSISTANCE.

There being no objection, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN left the meeting at 8:32 P.M. MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN chaired
the remainder of the meeting.

A.  PROPOSAL TO RETAIN WILLDAN ENGINEERING FOR 2021-22 STREET
  RESURFACING PROJECT (DESIGN & ENGINEERING SERVICES) AND TO ENTER
  INTO AN MOU WITH THE CITY OF RPV FOR SILVER SPUR RD.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba explained the proposed allocation
of funds, including $300,000 already budgeted for this fiscal year’s street resurfacing project,

  ABSTAIN:  Stegura

C.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM FROM MEETING OF AUGUST
  16, 2021 - CONCERT IN THE PARK

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Assistant City Manager Davis explained that the event would include half an hour pre-concert,
which would not interfere with any athletics occurring in different areas of the park, in response
COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

Assistant City Manager Davis explained that for events such as this, sponsorship dollars are
put into the Pepper Tree Foundation fund which are then used toward the event, in response
to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF supported the one-hour concert option for this single event, noting
that because other Peninsula cities offer similar concerts to the community, RHE may not need
to make this a regular event series.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN confirmed the 3:00 P.M. start time for the event.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE A ONE-HOUR CONCERT AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK WITH THE
  PALOS VERDES PENINSULA SYMPHONIC BAND ON SATURDAY,
  OCTOBER 23, 2021 IN THE AFTERNOON AT A COST OF $2,500.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
AUGUST 24, 2021
   AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Zuckerman

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer reported that the current Los Angeles County Health Officer Order is
still in effect requiring masks for all indoor public settings, regardless of vaccination status. A
new Health Officer Order has been issued effective August 23 requiring all attendees of large
outdoor events to wear masks regardless of vaccination status. Effective September 1, new
sports protocols will require certain infection control protocols be put in place including regular
testing. Also announced earlier this week, the FDA approved the Pfizer vaccine for those 16
and older, and booster vaccines are available for those who are immuno-compromised for
Pfizer and Moderna vaccines. There have been 27 new COVID cases in RHE since the last
City Council meeting on August 10. Vaccination rates continue to be very high in RHE, with
85.3% of people 12 and older having received at least one dose of the vaccine, 98% of those
aged 12-17, and 97.5% of those 65 and older.

The annual City Celebration will be held outdoors on Saturday, September 25 at the Empty
Saddle Club.

subcommittee will be working on the City Celebration plans for September 25.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also reported that the Peninsula Prepared Expo will be held on
Sunday, October 24 from 12:00 P.M. – 3:00 P.M.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN attended the Strategic Development session as an Executive
Board Member of the California Contract Cities Association (CCCA), where safety
requirements for the upcoming CCCA Fall Education Summit were discussed.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN also reported that he will be attending the Southern California
Association of Governments (SCAG) Community, Economic & Human Development
Committee and Emerging Technologies Committee meetings virtually this coming week.
